verdict: pass with corrections to the draft interpretation; the recommendation (no adoption, no default change, no merge) follows from the measured uncertainty
verdict_detail: The speed result is paired, mechanistically explained (fit-time saving equals search saving within 0.02-0.06), robust to the machine drift (within-pair bias at most about 3 percent), and consistent with intervals excluding 1 on five of six configurations. The accuracy result is descriptive: no target-metric combination reaches a two-sided sign p below 0.109, the trigger count is at its null expectation, the paired-difference ranges straddle zero everywhere except Student-t, and the rosenbrock n3 verdict reverses sign between the two pilot seeds and the eight continuation seeds. What weighs against S2 is the binary asymmetry (five convergence losses against none, one usability loss against nine gains, within-pair gsKL increases up to 103x) and the fact that frozen-state judging predicted none of it. That suffices to say S2 is not shown to be free of target-specific accuracy loss, the precondition the gate requires; it does not suffice to say a loss has been demonstrated. No default change, no adoption, no merge; follow-ups only as new declared allocations.
